newsitem.title: JAPAN: Iraqi envoy to visit Japan from March 17.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi envoy to visit Japan from March 17.

text.p: An Iraqi envoy who has been Baghdad's chief negotiator with the United Nations on an oil-for-food deal will visit Japan from March 17, the Japanese Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.

Abdul-Amir al-Anbari is due to meet Seiichiro Noboru, director-general of the ministry's Middle Eastern and African Affairs Bureau, to discuss sanctions imposed against Baghdad by the United Nations, a Foreign Ministry official said.
No firm date has yet been set for the meeting, he said.
It was unclear how long Anbari, who is Iraq's envoy to the Paris-based U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (Unesco), would be in Tokyo.
There are no plans for a meeting between Anbari and the foreign minister, the official said.
Anbari has led Iraq's talks on a U.N. agreement under which Baghdad has been allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian supplies.
A long-standing Iraqi objective is to secure the lifting of U.N. economic sanctions that have been in force since President Saddam Hussein's troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

Japan, a major importer of Iraqi crude before U.N. sanctions were imposed, has maintained that Iraq must abide by all U.N. Security Council resolutions for peace and security to return to the Gulf area.
It said that it would communicate its policy to the Iraqi envoy at the meeting.
